reading.body:
Apify is a web scraping and automation platform founded in 2015 and based in Prague, offering thousands of pre-built scrapers and crawlers through a marketplace model, with EU hosting and GDPR compliance.

The platform's value lies in its ability to extract structured data from websites at scale, which is foundational to training data pipelines. AI models require vast quantities of internet-sourced text, images, and structured information, and web scraping tools like Apify reduce the friction and cost of that collection. The marketplace model, where users can share and monetize scrapers, creates an ecosystem of reusable extraction logic rather than forcing each AI team to build crawlers from scratch.

This data does not reveal how much compute Apify consumes, how its infrastructure scales with demand, or whether it serves AI training pipelines specifically versus other enterprise use cases. The EU hosting and GDPR compliance are noted but the data does not explain the infrastructure implications, power usage, or whether these regulatory choices constrain the speed or scale at which data can be extracted and moved to training clusters.

profile_text.body:
Apify is a for-profit startup founded in 2015 and headquartered in Prague, Czech Republic. The company describes itself as operating the largest marketplace of trusted tools for AI, offering thousands of scrapers, crawlers, and automations through its Apify Store. Its platform is designed for web scraping and browser automation, with support for Python, JavaScript, and libraries including Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, Scrapy, and the company's own Crawlee library. The site emphasizes use cases such as real-time web data extraction, competitor tracking, lead generation, and app integration, and notes EU hosting and GDPR compliance.

Apify's AI-oriented offerings center on feeding crawled and cleaned web content into LLM applications, vector databases, and RAG pipelines, with stated integrations for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Its actors, which are the platform's discrete automation units, can extract structured data from sources such as Facebook pages, including posts, engagement metrics, video transcripts, and ad data, and can be scheduled or called via API. The company also publishes an MCP server, listed as com.apify/apify-mcp-server, allowing external AI agents to access its store of scrapers and automations.

The held facts record no litigation against the company. One noted collaboration referenced on the site involves applying Apify's tools to detect infringements of consumer protection legislation, though no specific organization is named in the available text.
